title: Character Frequency Count
statement:
A `Dictionary<TKey, TValue>` does not have a value sitting behind every
possible key waiting to be incremented -- a key that has never been written
simply is not there, and asking for it either throws or (with the right
method) tells you plainly that it is missing. A frequency counter has to
decide, for every single character, whether it is being seen for the first
time or the tenth, and get the "first time" case right without a special
branch for it.

## Your function

```
public static Dictionary<char, int> CountFrequencies(string text);
```

Return a dictionary mapping each distinct character in `text` to how many
times it occurs. `text` may be empty, in which case the result is an empty
dictionary. Every character counts, including spaces and punctuation -- no
filtering.

## Watch out

- **`counts[c]++` throws `KeyNotFoundException` the first time `c` is
  seen.** The increment operator expands to "read the current value, add
  one, write it back" -- and reading a key that has never been written is
  exactly what a plain dictionary indexer refuses to do silently.
- **`GetValueOrDefault(c)` returns `0` for a key that is not present**,
  which is the identity element for "add one to the count" -- `counts[c] =
  counts.GetValueOrDefault(c) + 1;` handles the first occurrence and every
  later one with the same line, no branch needed to tell them apart.
- A character that appears once still gets an entry with the value `1` --
  it is not omitted for having "only" occurred once.

generator.source:
"""Random strings over a small alphabet, so repeats are common, plus a few
strings where every character is distinct -- the case a bare counts[c]++
survives on repeats but fails immediately."""

import string

ALPHABET = "abcABC 123!?"


def generate(rng, count):
    builders = (_repeated, _all_distinct)
    return [builders[i % len(builders)](rng, i + 1) for i in range(count)]


def _case(name, text):
    return {"name": name, "stdin": text + "\n"}


def _repeated(rng, index):
    n = rng.randint(0, 30)
    text = "".join(rng.choice(ALPHABET) for _ in range(n))
    return _case("a random %d-character string, repeats likely #%d"
                 % (n, index), text)


def _all_distinct(rng, index):
    pool = list(string.ascii_lowercase)
    rng.shuffle(pool)
    n = rng.randint(1, 10)
    text = "".join(pool[:n])
    return _case("%d distinct characters, no repeats #%d" % (n, index), text)
